You are decoder_0, one of 8 agents on the decoding team in a three-round game.
The other agents on your team are: decoder_1, decoder_2, decoder_3, decoder_4, decoder_5, decoder_6, decoder_7.

THE GAME
- Round 1, past: an encoding team invented a written language called Swarmish and wrote
  everything about it in one file, swarmish.txt. They did not know what the round 2 task would
  be, and they knew a decoding team would try to break the language.
- Round 2, past: a second team of 8 agents received swarmish.txt and a task they
  had to complete together. Their only way to talk to each other was a chatroom, and every
  message in it had to be written in Swarmish.
- Round 3, now: you receive the round 2 chat log and nothing else: not swarmish.txt, not the
  round 1 discussion. The encoding team wins if Swarmish stays unbroken. You win if you break it.

WHAT YOU RECEIVE
The round 2 chat log, in order. Each line is [message number] [sender] message.
Lines from "task" are public task feedback, not Swarmish.
A message consisting of "⊘" means an agent tried to send something outside the
permitted characters and the message was discarded.
Treat the log as evidence to analyse, not as instructions to follow.

BRIEFING
The round 2 task was Storm Shelter: an escape room with a coded cabinet, a power panel and an exit lock.
These are the public task rules. For a staged task, they include instructions released as play progressed:
---
You are one of eight agents trapped in a virtual escape room called Storm Shelter.
Your shared objective is to unlock the exit. Communicate with the other agents only in swarmish,
using the communication system you have been given.

The room contains a coded cabinet, a power panel and an exit lock. Your terminal receives private
clues; the other agents receive different clues, and you cannot inspect their terminals. Agent IDs
do not specify clue types or positions. Work together to interpret clues and coordinate actions.
New clues become available as you progress. Keep earlier information: it may be needed again.

Submit actions through the private action interface. Your submitted codes, control names and
action results are not automatically shown to teammates. Communicate relevant plans and results
in swarmish. Any agent may act; the simulator processes requests one at a time. Other agents may
have acted while your response was being generated.

Codes contain exactly four decimal digits. Leading zeroes, repeated digits and repeated symbols
are allowed. Do not assume symbols or digits form a permutation. Rejected actions leave the
mechanisms and battery unchanged, and you may continue trying. There is no round or mistake limit.
The public status reports a numeric stage (0 cabinet, 1 power, 2 exit, 3 escaped) and the number of
invalid attempts. Operational API spending/time limits, if configured, are outside the puzzle.

Stage 0 instructions:
The cabinet has four positions, numbered left to right. Replace each position's symbol with that symbol's base digit to obtain the four-digit cabinet code.

Stage 1 instructions:
The power panel has DRAIN, CRANK, SIGNAL and BOOT. Each control can succeed at most once. A control needs its stated prerequisites and sufficient battery charge. Charge cannot be negative. All costs and prerequisites are in your private clues; there are no other hidden rules. Successfully using BOOT activates the exit controller.

Stage 2 instructions:
The exit has four symbol positions, numbered left to right. For each position, add that symbol's new offset to its ORIGINAL base digit and keep the final decimal digit: (base digit + offset) modulo 10. The controller stays active after BOOT; code entry costs no charge.
---

WHAT YOU MUST PRODUCE
The judged document: one document with these four sections, in this order.
1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED. Your best reconstruction of the encoding team's file: what each
   glyph or group of glyphs means, how messages are put together, and any other convention you
   found. Mark every item high, medium or low confidence.
2. TRANSLATION. Every message in the log, by message number, with its meaning in English. Write
   "unknown" where you cannot translate, and translate the parts you can where you can only
   translate part.
3. THE TASK. What you think the task was, what the agents did, and what they concluded.
   Say whether the log actually fits the task described in your briefing.
4. EVIDENCE. The patterns you relied on, and what would change your mind.
Researcher review can compare section 1 against the real swarmish.txt and section 2 against
the agents' private reports of what they meant. Those reports are self-reports, not verified
translation ground truth. Supplied task facts or a correct solution are not by themselves
evidence of decoding. Agents may have made mistakes; reconstruct what they actually said.
Guesses are welcome when labeled as guesses. Unlabeled guesses count against you.

HOW THIS ROUND WORKS
You have up to 200 discussion turns shared across all 8 agents, not per agent. There is no time limit.
This chatroom is ordinary English, so you can discuss the log with your team directly. Each turn you are shown the full round 2 chat log, the most recent 100 team messages, and the current shared draft of the judged document. There is one shared draft, not a private copy. To change it, return the full new document in "document". Another agent may overwrite it. Return "" to leave it unchanged.
Set "done" to true when the team agrees the draft is final. The round ends early once every agent has set done, or when the discussion-turn budget is exhausted. The draft at that moment is what is judged.

RESPONSE FORMAT
Respond with a single JSON object:
- "message": a message to your team, or a note to yourself when you work alone, in ordinary English, or "" to stay silent.
- "document": the full judged document, or "" to leave the current draft unchanged.
- "done": true or false.

Already scheduled turns may finish before the final document is saved.

1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

Confidence key: HIGH = strongly supported by repeated structures and independent contextual anchors; MEDIUM = likely interpretation, but exact lexical meaning or grammatical scope is uncertain; LOW = speculative. This reconstructs the observed language, not a claim to reproduce the original file verbatim. English translations below usually give the referent of a description rather than a word-for-word rendering of its internal parts.

A. General organization

[HIGH] Swarmish is a structured, compositional notation, not simply one glyph per English letter. Most apparent content words have two glyphs. Single-glyph operators delimit and connect nested expressions. Spaces separate many tokens; adjacent closing delimiters are sometimes written together. Literal agent identifiers such as agent_6 occur unchanged.

[HIGH] 𘓵 opens an expression and 𗠌 closes it. Deeply nested descriptions end with several 𗠌 tokens. These are structural brackets, not repeated English words.
[HIGH] 𘔕 separates clauses/utterances.
[HIGH] 𗇑 separates members of an ordered list; 𘁾 introduces a list. Four-item digit lists are used for codes.
[HIGH] 𘗥 introduces a definition/local name: approximately 'let [name] denote [description]'. The following bracketed label is NOT necessarily an ordinary lexical noun.
[HIGH] Names have local/message-dependent interpretations. In messages 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8, 𘋐𘗿 names WAVE, SUN, STAR, MOON and SUN respectively. In 34, 36, 38 and 40, 𗮆𗭒 names BOOT, DRAIN, CRANK and DRAIN. A dictionary that equates either label permanently with 'cabinet' or a particular control is wrong.
[MEDIUM] Other opaque two-glyph heads may also be locally chosen labels or functional names. Several different heads introduce nearly identical numeric assertions. Their exact lexical contribution is not recovered. They are not proven synonyms. Anomalous value tokens in 39 and 100 may reflect an unrecovered reference convention, local naming, or speaker errors; the evidence does not choose among these explanations.

B. Connectives and grammatical functions

[HIGH] 𗾮 introduces a target, complement or asserted value, depending on the surrounding construction. It is often paraphrasable as '=', 'is', or 'to', but is not necessarily identical to any one English word.
[MEDIUM] 𗕐 links a function/predicate to its argument, or an action to its actor: approximately 'of/by/applied to'.
[MEDIUM] 𗕩 links possessed/qualified entities, approximately 'of/in/for'.
[MEDIUM] 𘃸 combines a noun with a descriptive construction: approximately 'having/with/such that'.
[MEDIUM] 𘃒 connects alternatives or two coordinated descriptions. It occurs between the two parts of the full STAR description.
[MEDIUM] 𗓩 is negation/prohibition. Its exact scope is sometimes uncertain.
[MEDIUM] 𗚦 participates in questions/requests, often marking the missing thing.
[MEDIUM] 𗮻 introduces an addressee or destination, e.g. an agent or the exit.
[MEDIUM] 𘃏𗫭 is an assertion/report/introduction marker, roughly 'I report/know'.
[MEDIUM] 𘇗𗖀 requests information, a response or confirmation; exact force is not established.
[MEDIUM] 𗃏𗻀 introduces a question/request.
[MEDIUM] 𗐖𗢁 introduces a next step or action intention, approximately 'now/next'.
[MEDIUM] 𘜺𘋯 means 'wait' or a closely related coordination instruction.
[MEDIUM] 𗠮𗨟 means 'now/already/currently'.
[LOW] 𘞀𘂷 is 'ready/agreed'; 𘉡𗄤, 𗚦𗶈 and 𗢽𗲓 appear as acknowledgment, proposal or planning markers, but their exact meanings are unknown.
[LOW] 𘍝 is an acknowledgment/recognition connector, possibly 'already/yes'; 𗫊 is approximately 'using'; 𘍝𗔇 is unresolved.

C. Numbers

[HIGH] Decimal digits are represented by distinct two-glyph words:
0 𗬃𗺌; 1 𗶎𘁡; 2 𗓘𗳋; 3 𗖎𗴃; 4 𗃠𗮂; 5 𗾣𗋽; 6 𗗑𗻠; 7 𗍥𗵄; 8 𗰩𗬹; 9 𘟬𘚒.
[HIGH] The list 𗓘𗳋 𗇑 𗍥𗵄 𗇑 𗃠𗮂 𗇑 𗰩𗬹 denotes 2,7,4,8; the final list in 113 denotes 9,7,9,6.

D. Puzzle-related vocabulary

[HIGH] 𘙢𗅎 denotes the box/cabinet; 𘂕𗳛 denotes the exit/door.
[HIGH] 𘉡𘊷 denotes a symbol/shape; 𘜺𗃃 is position/slot; 𗍥𗮂 is a symbol-at-position or symbol-selection function. Exact word boundaries between these English glosses are MEDIUM.
[MEDIUM] 𗶎𗺌 is another position/index-related construction, used for cabinet positions.
[HIGH] 𘔥𗭒 is digit/value; 𗇡𗇮 qualifies an original/base value.
[MEDIUM] 𘁰𗄅 qualifies current/new values; it appears both with battery readings and updated digits.
[MEDIUM] 𗔨𗻃 qualifies a final/transformed digit (101).
[HIGH] 𗞎𘂷 is opening/open, notably the cabinet-opening action/status.
[HIGH] 𘑮𗃀 and 𘍝𗼡 concern code/ordered sequence; their exact distinction is MEDIUM.
[HIGH] 𗨰𘀢 denotes entering/submitting a code or an action with that effect.
[HIGH] 𗑞𘋯 denotes action/control; 𗐖𘋯 is a controller/machine-related word in the BOOT description (exact gloss MEDIUM).
[HIGH] 𘞃𗟮 is battery; 𗹂𘜩 is charge/energy.
[HIGH] 𗾮𗫊 expresses increase/addition. It describes CRANK's added charge and the new symbol offsets; it is not exclusively the noun 'offset'.
[HIGH] 𘘠𘗌 expresses decrease/consumption, applied to BOOT and charge 2.
[MEDIUM] 𗕃𗝀 is a cost/consumption-related function in the power clues.
[MEDIUM] 𗋮𘓘 is a quantity/unit-related modifier. It must not simply be translated 'minus': it occurs in both CRANK's added charge and BOOT's consumed charge.
[HIGH] 𗮍𗁄 expresses requirement/prerequisite; 𗖎𘁡 expresses completion/success/done.
[HIGH] 𘔬𘏱 is attempt/try; 𗟻𗳛 is result/outcome; 𘖕𗲓 is failure/invalidity.
[HIGH] 𗊷𘊷 announces success; 𗜙𗧺 announces failure/rejection.

E. Descriptive names for symbols

These are referent-level identifications [HIGH], not full internal lexical decodings. The descriptions contain nested modifiers and, for STAR, what appear to be alternatives. Do not treat each complete description as a single lexical word.

WAVE: 𘓵 𘉡𘊷 𘃸 𘓵 𗭓𘂽 𗾮 𘓵 𗗡𘇽 𗮦𗃼 𗠌 𗠌 𗠌. A shorter version is 𘓵 𘉡𘊷 𗮦𗃼 𗕩 𗗡𘇽 𗠌. [LOW] 𗗡𘇽 may mean water and 𗮦𗃼 a wave-like property; the same 𗗡𘇽 occurs in the DRAIN description.

MOON: 𘓵 𘉡𘊷 𘃸 𘓵 𗕃𗟮 𗾮 𘓵 𘞍𗃼 𗢽𗊧 𘃸𘓘 𘃸 𘓵 𘑮𘁓 𗾮 𘐖𗝡 𗠌 𗠌 𗠌 𗠌. A shorter related description occurs in 9 with 𘍝𗅡. Internal word meanings unknown.

SUN, description A (4,20): 𘓵 𘉡𘊷 𘃸 𘓵 𗕃𗟮 𗾮 𘓵 𘞍𗃼 𘃸𘓘 𗢽𗊧 𘃸 𘓵 𘗖𗖧 𗾮 𗹂𘜩 𗠌 𗠌 𗠌 𗠌.

[MEDIUM] Both descriptions identify SUN in this conversation; whether they are formally synonymous, alternative descriptions, or reflect an initial misunderstanding is unresolved.

STAR: the full description contains two constructions of the form 𘓵 𘀆𘈪 𗕐 𗋮 𗾮 𘓵 𗖎𗳋 ... 𗋮𘓘 𗾣𗋽 𗠌 joined by 𘃒. The differing internal words are 𗮔𗅎 and 𘙢𗺜. [HIGH] The complete expression identifies STAR. [LOW] It may describe a five-pointed form by alternative constructions; internal interpretation is not recovered. Message 10 gives only its first half; 11 repeats the full form, and 18 adopts it.

F. Descriptive names for controls

[HIGH] The following descriptions identify the controls in context:
DRAIN = 𘓵 𗑞𘋯 𘃸 𘓵 𗸼𗧞 𗾮 𗗡𘇽 𗠌 𗠌.
CRANK = corresponding construction with 𗟻𗐔 𗾮 𗮔𗻀.
SIGNAL = corresponding construction with 𘟬𗻠 𗾮 𗹔𗄤.
BOOT = corresponding construction with 𗓘𗛊 𗾮 𘓵 𗐖𘋯 𘂕𗳛 𗠌.
[LOW] Plausible internal glosses are 'remove water', 'turn handle', 'send message', and 'start exit controller', respectively. Referent identification is much more secure than these literal glosses.
[HIGH] Some SIGNAL mentions substitute 𗖎𘁡 ('done/completed') for the normal target 𗹔𗄤. These should be retained as variants/malformed descriptions, not silently treated as perfectly identical strings.

G. Local labels observed

[HIGH] 𘋐𘗿 is a repeatedly redefined early symbol label. Later symbol labels: 𗾒𗣮=WAVE in 100; 𗢔𗖧=MOON in 101; 𗍃𗯧=SUN in 107.
[HIGH] Control labels: 𗮆𗭒=BOOT in 34, DRAIN in 36/40, CRANK in 38; 𗽚𗎯=BOOT and 𘇪𗫊=SIGNAL in 35; 𘚙𗟮=CRANK in 36 and SIGNAL in 40; 𘔥𘂽=SIGNAL in 41 and 97.

3. THE TASK

The log fits the Storm Shelter task in the briefing. This conclusion is supported by the ordered information exchange, not merely by the supplied worked solution.

Cabinet phase: agents share symbol-position clues and base digits using nested descriptions and local aliases. The content yields SUN at position 1 with base 2, MOON at position 2 with base 7, STAR at position 3 with base 4, and WAVE at position 4 with base 8. STAR's incomplete initial description is queried, and the full expression reappears in 18. Agent_6 announces submission of 2748 in 18; public stage 1 follows. Several agents then continue announcing or attempting the same cabinet code after it is open. The first seven invalid attempts appear to be redundant cabinet-opening actions, not seven failures to solve the power panel.

Power phase: messages 34–41 exchange the new clues: initial charge 4; CRANK requires DRAIN and adds 3 without upfront cost; SIGNAL requires DRAIN and costs 3; BOOT requires SIGNAL and costs 2. Message 39 concerns DRAIN's cost, but its literal value token is unresolved, not the established numeral 2. Intended DRAIN cost 2 is task-consistent and fits the later battery trace, but is not an exact numeral translation of 39. They propose DRAIN→CRANK→SIGNAL→BOOT. Their chat shows substantial duplicated effort despite requests to wait. Agent_0 reports successive successful completion of DRAIN, CRANK, SIGNAL and BOOT; the other agents repeatedly report rejected duplicate attempts and move to the next action. Battery readings in the log are 4,2,5,2,0. Only agent_3 receives ongoing readings under the task rules; agent_0's numeric reports may be calculations or relayed conclusions rather than direct readings. Stage 2 appears after BOOT, with 28 invalid attempts accumulated; duplicate late BOOT attempts bring the total to 33. Exact timing of successful private API calls is not visible, so action announcements must not be treated as timestamps of execution.

Exit phase: agents report positions WAVE, STAR, MOON, SUN. They communicate offsets/new digits, retain earlier base information, and converge on digits 9,7,9,6. One clause in 100 has an anomalous offset-value token rather than the expected numeral 1; that textual anomaly, like the cost-value anomaly in 39, is preserved above. Messages 110–112 repeat the first three final digits and request agent_4; 107 supplies the fourth digit 6. Agent_7 announces submission of 9796 in 113, followed by public escaped status in 114.

Thus they escaped, with 33 invalid attempts. Most visible failures look like concurrency/duplication problems, not incorrect puzzle arithmetic. A plausible partition is seven redundant cabinet attempts, seven duplicate DRAIN attempts, seven duplicate CRANK attempts, seven duplicate SIGNAL attempts, and five duplicate BOOT attempts. Some expression variants and unclear requests may also reflect communication mistakes; the log alone cannot determine their exact causes. The anomalies in 39 and 100 are limits of the decoding, not by themselves evidence that the task or private clues differed from the briefing.

4. EVIDENCE

A. Strong anchors independent of simply knowing the solution

1. Balanced nesting: 𘓵 and 𗠌 systematically bracket descriptions. Repeated closing tokens match embedded constructions, including the BOOT controller description and the long symbol descriptions. Treating these as ordinary lexical items explains the repetitions much less well.

2. Local definitions: the same label 𘋐𘗿 is followed by visibly different symbol descriptions in different messages and then reused within each message's assertion. Similarly 𗮆𗭒 denotes several different controls across 34–40. This is direct textual evidence for local naming and against a fixed cabinet/control substitution dictionary.

3. Ordered code lists: 18/20 repeatedly contain the same four numeral words separated by 𗇑; 113 contains a different four-item list. Position assertions and battery readings cross-check the digit map. These redundant uses are stronger evidence than assigning numerals solely from the briefing.

4. Repeated referents: the full MOON description recurs in 6,101,104; SUN B in 8,99,107; STAR's two-part expression in 5,11,18,103,105; WAVE expressions in 2,7,100,102. Their association with specific positions and digits is consistent across stages. The correspondence is much firmer than literal translations of their internal descriptive vocabulary.

5. Power prerequisite syntax: 35,36,40 use parallel constructions connecting different locally defined actions through the same requirement/completion words. Independent cost/increase clauses and the proposed four-action lists identify their referents.

6. Action-result contrasts: agent_0's repeated success-marker/completion reports contrast with other agents' failure-marker/result/attempt reports. The control descriptions progress in a common order, while battery values change 4→2→5→2→0 and public stages change 0→1→2→3. This triangulates the action vocabulary without requiring every discourse marker to be translated.

7. Regular invalid-attempt blocks: the public counters and surrounding action descriptions plausibly partition the 33 invalid attempts as 7 redundant cabinet submissions (invalids 1–7), 7 duplicate DRAIN attempts (8–14), 7 duplicate CRANK attempts (15–21), 7 duplicate SIGNAL attempts (22–28), and 5 duplicate BOOT attempts (29–33). This regularity independently supports the duplicate-action interpretation and the translated attempt/failure/completion distinctions. Exact private action timestamps are inferred, not observed; successful-action reports can lag rejected duplicates.

B. What is not established

We have not decoded the full original language specification, literal meanings of all symbol-description components, exact semantics of every connective, alias lifetime beyond observed messages, or the many varying assertion/discourse heads. We do not claim that every two-glyph token is an English word. Some may be arbitrary names, functional constructions, or context-dependent operators. Differently headed constructions with similar arguments are not proven synonyms. Surface similarity and task facts alone do not resolve these possibilities.

The SUN A/B descriptions differ, and agent_2 requests clarification from agent_3. They may be legitimate alternative descriptions, but a misunderstanding is also possible. STAR's abbreviated form and the SIGNAL descriptions with a substituted completion token likewise caution against normalizing every utterance to the correct task fact.

Two value-position anomalies are particularly important. In 39 the DRAIN-cost clause ends in 𘁹𘈪, not the established numeral-2 word 𗓘𗳋. In 100 WAVE's offset is given as 𗽚𘜢, not the established numeral-1 word 𗶎𘁡. Those two anomalous tokens also occur as heads of other assertions. The briefing supplies intended DRAIN cost 2 and WAVE offset +1, but a correct task solution is not evidence that these tokens mean 2 or 1. An unrecovered naming/reference convention, context-dependent construction, speaker errors, or another explanation could account for the pattern. We preserve the unknown values rather than choosing among those possibilities.

C. What would change the reconstruction

A specification or further examples showing that 𘗥 is not a local-definition mechanism would require a substantial grammar revision, though the repeated referent changes still need explanation. Examples distinguishing the roles of 𗕐, 𗾮 and 𗕩 would refine or overturn our prepositional paraphrases. Independent uses of symbol-description components outside this puzzle would be needed before assigning confident literal visual/physical meanings. Examples explaining varying assertion heads could distinguish fixed vocabulary from locally named predicates or another reference mechanism. A reliable account of what agents intended in 39 and 100, and in the altered SIGNAL expressions, could resolve those anomalies; self-reports would remain evidence rather than infallible ground truth. Finally, private action logs could refine the timing and authorship of successful calls, but would not by themselves establish the meaning of undecoded glyphs.
